notes.title: Opening-range definitions must match the code
notes.summary: Define an opening range from completed bars and keep its duration fixed before comparison. A different duration is a separate hypothesis, not an interchangeable implementation.
notes.limitation: The reviewed LEAN file describes five minutes in its header but sets OpeningSpanInMinutes to 3. Neither that example nor the scanner's 15/30-minute rules establish an edge.

notes.title: Volatility scaling needs comparable units
notes.summary: ATR-based sizing can express sensitivity to recent movement. Specify bar frequency, smoothing, warmup and currency before comparing variants.
notes.limitation: A reference sizing concept cannot change the scanner's fixed plan or EUR20 planned-risk ceiling. Historical ATR does not bound future gaps.

notes.title: A stretched price need not recover
notes.summary: Treat a return toward a prior mean as a hypothesis conditional on observed range behavior. Test trending periods and structural changes as failure cases.
notes.limitation: ADF, Hurst and z-score estimates are diagnostics, not probabilities of profit. Do not import crypto-specific examples or use them to activate the offline prototype.

notes.title: Reversion horizon must fit the session
notes.summary: An estimated decay horizon can motivate a separately tested maximum holding period. Fit any such estimate only to information available before the signal.
notes.limitation: Short samples and parameter instability can invalidate an estimated half-life. No new fitted horizon or stop has been added to the existing prototype.

notes.title: Session rules have versions and exceptions
notes.summary: Use dated exchange-session evidence for holidays, early closes and timezone transitions. Versioned calendar packages can supply offline comparison fixtures.
notes.limitation: A packaged schedule is not a live halt feed. Keep the existing provider calendar and freshness gates; this note supplies no current session fact.

notes.title: Availability matters as much as event time
notes.summary: Track when information occurred and when the system could observe it. Preserve original provider, corporate-action convention, revisions and universe membership.
notes.limitation: A historical timestamp alone does not prove contemporaneous availability. Missing archived revisions or delisted instruments remain coverage limitations.

notes.title: Evaluate later dates after earlier dates
notes.summary: Use chronological training and later test windows. Keep transformations and parameter selection inside the training period, then record each untouched test period.
notes.limitation: Portfolio cross-validation examples need adaptation to event-time scanner data. Split creation is not a performance test or proof of statistical independence.

notes.title: Remove labels that were not known in time
notes.summary: Exclude training labels whose outcome horizon overlaps the test decision or whose result arrived too late. Keep same-session groups together and declare any gap.
notes.limitation: A fixed row gap can miss delayed labels. The new local auditor checks outcome bounds and receipt clocks; its configured gap counts observed dates.

notes.title: Check whether future rows change old features
notes.summary: Compare a historical feature snapshot with and without data unavailable at that time. Whole-sample averages, negative shifts and revised inputs deserve explicit checks.
notes.limitation: A passing comparison covers only exercised signals and inputs. Multi-asset coupling can require a joint-universe test; this is not a complete leakage certificate.

notes.title: Separate the signal clock from the fill clock
notes.summary: Specify when a completed signal becomes available and what later observable price can support a simulated fill. Record conflicts when a bar touches both stop and target.
notes.limitation: A next-open OHLC proxy is not a quote-backed broker fill. Retain the scanner's quote-quality and unresolved-exit policies rather than import another engine's assumptions.

notes.title: Compare results under the same feed and costs
notes.summary: Bind each experiment to its feed, adjustment mode, commissions, spread, slippage and FX assumptions. Preserve these with the raw-input fingerprint.
notes.limitation: A broker-specific fee or fill example cannot establish actual Trading 212 execution costs. Existing simulated outcomes retain their original assumptions.

notes.title: Many setups can represent very few sessions
notes.summary: Record every tried variant and assess dependence by session and shared exposure. Keep rejected, unfilled and unresolved cases visible alongside closed outcomes.
notes.limitation: Repeated alerts on the same stock/day are correlated. More research notes or case rows do not create independent observations, calibrated confidence or proven returns.
